newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH H197 NEW CAR SALES UP 20 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH H197 NEW CAR SALES UP 20 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: New passenger car sales in the Czech Republic rose in the first half of 1997 to 89,795 from 74,792 while imports rose to 40,081 from 32,804, compared with the same period of 1996, the Czech Car Importers Association (CIA) said on Thursday.
It said the sale of light utility vehicles rose overall 13.5 percent year-on-year to 10,168 while imports of those vehicles rose 16.8 percent to 7,187.
The figures do not include imports by individuals.

The CIA said in a statement that import growth in the first half of this year had been slower than in the first half of 1996. This was mainly due to longer waits for delivery and the negative influence of changes in the crown rate.
The importers' share of the new car market dropped to 44.64 percent in the first half of 1997 from 46.2 percent in the first half of 1996.

In terms of new sales, domestic producer Skoda Automobilova a.s., a unit of Volkswagen AG , held the biggest share, with 55.34 percent of the market for passenger vehicles, or 49,693 cars, in the first half.
The leading importer was Ford with 5,452 new passenger cars sold, followed by Opel with 4,548 and Volkswagen on 3,888.
Skoda's share of the market dropped from 56.08 percent for the same period of last year.
